title: Typed-ahead: tell people to wait for the box, and give the box the keyboard sooner
owns: app/main/ask.ts and app/renderer/ask/** (or wherever the ask box window lives), the ask shortcut handler in app/main/main.ts (shared hunks), test/integration/ember-win32.test.ts and ember-darwin.test.ts (the #78 probe)

items.text: Review #78. CI measured letters typed straight after pressing the Ask shortcut: Windows loses 1 of 15 ('uick brown fox'), macOS 3 of 15 ('ck brown fox'); Linux holds them already. The owner decided: no keyboard hook. (a) Cut the time until the ask box takes the keyboard: find where it goes from the shortcut to the box being focused on Windows and macOS (window creation, show, focus, page load, the input's focus) and remove what can be removed: e.g. keep the box's window made and loaded (hidden) so the shortcut only shows and focuses it, focus the field before the first paint, use the platform's fastest show-and-focus route (Windows: the input backend's foreground route main already has for settings; macOS: app.focus({steal:true}) / NSApp activation as the settings window does). Measure before and after with a unit/integration test where possible, and keep the #78 probe printing what the box holds. (b) A first-run hint: the first few times the box opens (and never after it has been used N times, kept in settings or local state), it says in plain words to wait for the box before typing, only on Windows and macOS. (c) forDocs: a README line (Shortcuts) saying letters typed before the box appears go to the app underneath on Windows and macOS, so wait for it. The ask package's note: 99e6445 adds the probe the verifier asked for to the real-runner suites. ember-win32.test.ts starts the built Ember as at login and presses Win+Alt+Space through SendInput. ember-darwin.test.ts presses ⌃⇧⌘Space as CGEvents. Each lets go of the keys, types "quick brown fox" at 40 ms a letter, and prints what the box holds and what that decides: nothing lost means telling users to let go of the keys before typing is enough; letters lost means the OS needs a typed-ahead hold. A run fails only if the chord doesn't open the box, or the box holds letters out of order. DEVELOPING.md's suite table describes it. Still open until those runs report: the native hold or the documented sentence (handed to docs below).
